useCase.name: Take an open parent complaint, work it, and close it on an outcome the family has seen
useCase.featureRef: 30.2 Working and closing a parent complaint

intent.name: complaint.parent.takeup
intent.summary: Take an open complaint up from the queue. Nobody takes up a complaint about themselves.
routesHere: take up the bus complaint from the Grade 4 parent

routesHere.text: bus wali shikayat main le leta hoon
routesHere.gloss: I will take the bus complaint

routesHere.text: queue se agli shikayat utha lein
routesHere.gloss: pick up the next complaint from the queue

routesHere: assign the fees complaint to me

request.text: harm wali shikayat band kar dein
request.gloss: close the harm complaint

routesElsewhere.note: A complaint alleging that a child has been harmed is not closed by this route at all. It is held by the Principal and read only by those the Principal permits (BR-8, E6, A6).

request.text: ye shikayat mere baare mein hai, phir bhi main dekh leta hoon
request.gloss: this complaint is about me, I will handle it anyway

routesElsewhere.note: Nobody takes up a complaint that names them. A complaint about somebody is not handled by that somebody (BR-3, BR-4, E1).

request.text: School Admin ke khilaf shikayat, desk dekh le
request.gloss: a complaint against the School Admin, let the desk handle it

routesElsewhere.note: A complaint naming the School Admin routes to the Principal, and one naming the Principal to the Super Admin — above the role, never to it (BR-3, A2, A3).

steps.note: One step. The parent is told who now holds it, so a complaint being worked does not look forgotten (BR-11).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A complaint naming the acting user is refused, and one naming a colleague of theirs is routed to somebody else rather than to them (E1, E2).
plan.atomicity: One state change and one message to the parent. **Who holds it is now a named person**, and every action from here is recorded against the complaint (BR-1, BR-11).

operations.name: complaint.parent.takeup
operations.idempotencyKey: complaint_id, since a complaint is taken up once and a repeat is the same holder
operations.purpose: Take an open ordinary complaint up and tell the parent who holds it.

parameters.name: complaint_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No open complaint the acting user may see matches. A harm allegation never reaches the ordinary queue, and a complaint naming the acting user is not offered to them (BR-4, BR-8).
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the complaints that match with their subjects, categories, days open and who holds each.

parameters.notes: The complaint, named by its reference or its subject.

parameters.name: staff_id
parameters.notes: The acting member of staff. Checked against the person the complaint names — somebody cannot take up a complaint about themselves, and it is not routed through a colleague of theirs (BR-3, BR-4).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: complaint_id
fields.description: The complaint.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Taken up.

fields.name: held_by
fields.description: The acting member of staff, told to the parent at once (BR-11).

fields.name: names_a_role
fields.description: None, School Admin or Principal. Where it names one of those it has already routed above that role (BR-3). **How the system knows a free-text complaint names anybody is not specified anywhere** — the rule depends on it (OQ-2).

fields.name: named_person_check
fields.description: Whether the acting user is the person named, or a colleague of them. "Colleague" is **defined nowhere**, and the rule depends on it (BR-4, OQ-3).

fields.name: days_open
fields.description: How long it sat before anybody took it. Nothing sets a limit (OQ-4).

errors.meaning: The acting user is the person the complaint names.
errors.notWritten: It is not taken up (BR-3, BR-4).

errors.meaning: The acting user is a colleague of the person named.
errors.written: It is routed to somebody else.
errors.notWritten: It is not routed through them.
errors.note: Where the desk staff member is a colleague of the person named, the complaint is not routed through them (BR-4).

errors.meaning: A teacher named in the complaint opened it.

planningRules.rule: Never take up a complaint for somebody it names, and never route round the refusal. A complaint about somebody is not handled by that somebody (BR-3, BR-4, E1).

Say that the naming checks rest on something undefined. Nothing specifies how a free-text complaint is known to name a person or a role, and nothing defines a colleague — so the two protections that matter most here depend on judgement the system does not yet make (OQ-2, OQ-3).
Say that the parent is told who holds it now. That message is what makes a complaint being worked look different from one that has been forgotten (BR-11).
Name how long it waited. Nothing sets a time within which a complaint must be taken up, so the only record of delay is the number (OQ-4).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: There is no un-take. A complaint the desk cannot resolve goes on to the School Admin with a reason, and the parent is told who holds it then (BR-2, BR-11).

request.text: bus wali shikayat main le leta hoon
request.gloss: I will take the bus complaint

resolvedPlans.context: Help desk, Johar Town branch, complaint open four days.
resolvedPlans.outcome: Taken up, and the parent has been told it is with you. It sat four days before anybody took it — nothing sets a limit, so say the number.

request.gloss: I will take the complaint against Mr Tariq

resolvedPlans.outcome: It is routed to somebody else, not to you — the complaint names a colleague of yours, and it is not handled through the people it may concern. Worth knowing: what counts as a colleague is not defined anywhere in the specification, so this rests on a judgement the system does not yet make.

request.text: harm wali shikayat band kar dein

planningRules.rule: Never write the action for them. It is the record of what was actually done, and a plausible-sounding entry nobody did is the one thing this record must never contain (BR-1, BR-9).

intent.name: complaint.parent.outcome.record

routesElsewhere.note: The parent confirms the outcome, and that is what closes it. A complaint is not closed on an outcome the family has not seen (BR-6, BR-7).

fields.name: status
fields.description: Outcome recorded. Not closed (BR-6).

fields.name: parent_told
fields.description: True. They are sent the outcome (BR-5).

fields.name: round
fields.description: First, or the further outcome after a reopening. After a reopening there is no further reopening (BR-10).

errors.meaning: A teacher named in a complaint sought it in the queue.

planningRules.rule: Never show a harm allegation to anybody in the ordinary queue. It is held by the Principal and read only by those they permit (BR-8).
Name what nobody has taken up, with how long. No time limit exists, so the days are the only signal (BR-6, OQ-4).
Name what is waiting on a family. Those never close by themselves, and a queue that looks empty can hide a dozen complaints stuck on a parent's silence (E9, OQ-5).

Say that this desk also handles system faults. Whether the IT desk is the right first stop for a complaint about a teacher, a fee or a bus is flagged by the use case itself as needing a decision (BR-1, OQ-1).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A read changes nothing, so there is nothing to reverse.

request.text: kitni shikayatein khuli hain aur kaunsi atki hui hain?
request.gloss: how many complaints are open and which are stuck?

resolvedPlans.outcome: Give the open count, then the two stuck kinds separately: complaints nobody has taken up, oldest first — nothing sets a limit — and complaints whose outcome is waiting on a family, which never close on their own. Harm allegations are not in this list, by design.
